turn_history.text: I have: Which of these shows part of the proof that the sum of two odd numbers is even? I got \( \begin{array}{l}2 n+(2 m+1) \\ =2(n+m)+1\end{array} \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The mistake in your calculation is that you are treating 2n as an odd number. Remember, 2n represents an even number because it is divisible by 2. So, the correct step should be \(2(n+m) + 1\). Keep in mind that when adding two odd numbers, the result is always even.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so 2n is even because it's got the 2 in front... but I'm still a bit confused about why we'd start with 2n if we're trying to prove that two odd numbers add up to even? Shouldn't both of them be odd at the start?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The reason we start with 2n in the proof is to show that even when one of the numbers is even (2n), the sum of two odd numbers will still result in an even number. It's important to remember that in mathematics, we use different numbers in our proofs to demonstrate general properties and relationships. Keep practicing to strengthen your understanding of these concepts.
